activities.caption: pair each lineage with its devotion
activities.name: hindSampradayaMatch

config.prompt: Before the single-word umbrella, insiders identified by sampradaya — pair lineage and devotion:
config.why: Each lineage keeps its own texts, rituals and theologians — related the way Protestant denominations and Catholic orders are, or rather more loosely. The umbrella word crystallised under colonial administration: censuses and law codes needed one box.

activities.caption: true or false — the many and the one
activities.name: hindGodsJudge

statements.s: Practised Hinduism is a crowd of rival gods in the naive sense.
statements.why: Polytheistic in form, yes — but the many deities are widely understood as faces, manifestations or emanations of one ultimate reality or one supreme God.

statements.s: 'Truth is one; the wise call it by many names' comes from the Rig Veda.
statements.why: Rig Veda 1.164.46 — the sentence the lesson uses to name the interpretation.

statements.s: Different households and lineages disagree about which face is primary — and tradition treats the dispute as heresy.
statements.why: The disagreement is licensed, not heretical — categories drawn from one tradition rarely fit another.

statements.s: 'Hindu' began as a Persian geographical term for people beyond the Indus river.
statements.why: A location, not a faith — the word later crystallised into a single-box umbrella.

activities.caption: file the library — heard or remembered?
activities.name: hindShrutiSort

config.prompt: Shruti ('heard' — revealed) vs smriti ('remembered' — authored): file each text:

items.label: the four Vedas — Rig, Sama, Yajur, Atharva
the Upanishads (c. 800–200 BCE) — where Atman meets Brahman
the Brahmanas and Aranyakas — ritual manuals, forest teachings
the Mahabharata — the world's longest poem
the Puranas — the mythological encyclopaedia most Hindus learned from
the dharma literature — law codes like the Manusmriti

config.why: The Gita lives inside the Mahabharata — smriti, however exalted. Authority runs through the Vedas first; the library is layered, not a single volume.

config.prompt: The classical scheme builds the arc into a life — order the ashrama:
items: Householder — live fully: prosperity and pleasure, governed by duty
config.why: Strikingly non-ascetic: wealth (artha) and pleasure (kama) are legitimate aims of the classical four, as long as dharma governs them — 'live fully first, then turn inward'.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the temple visit
activities.name: hindPujaSpot

config.prompt: One line of this temple-visit description is wrong — click it:
lines: The temple is built as the deity's palace — the tower over the garbhagriha replicates the cosmic mountain.
The murti is an 'idol' in the polemical sense — a mere statue to be avoided.
The murti is consecrated, honoured, fed and dressed.
The home shrine makes the same logic daily.
The festivals mark the calendar: Diwali, Holi, Navaratri — and the Kumbh Mela draws tens of millions.
config.correction: The murti is not an 'idol' in the polemical sense — it is a focus of presence: consecrated, honoured, fed, dressed.
config.why: The theology: God, who is everywhere, consents to be met here. Puja is devotional honouring, not idolatry.

activities.anchor: In the tradition the word names
activities.caption: drag between the fitness export and Patanjali
activities.name: hindYogaCompare

config.prompt: Two things the word 'yoga' has named — drag the divider:

before.label: The global export
before.text: Posture-centred practice — real, recent, and a partial descendant: a fitness regime, often with the philosophy thinned away.

after.label: Patanjali's system
after.text: A psychology of attention: yoga defined as the stilling of the mind's fluctuations; eight limbs with only one on posture — originally a steady seat for meditation — breath, withdrawal, concentration and absorption doing the rest.

config.why: One of the six classical philosophies — a soteriology of attention — of which the modern fitness practice is a recent, real, but partial descendant.

activities.anchor: The tradition's history is a succession
activities.caption: scrub the arc — sacrifice to devotion
activities.name: hindArcTimeline

events.title: Vedic religion
events.text: Sacrificial: the fire ritual maintaining cosmic order through precise offering — expert-dominated, Brahmin-led.

events.title: The Upanishadic turn
events.text: Interiorised: meditation and knowledge replace sacrifice as the royal road (c. 800–200 BCE).

events.title: Epics and the Gita
events.text: Householder religion institutionalised; the Bhagavad Gita (c. 200 BCE–200 CE) distils the philosophy of action.

events.title: Bhakti in the Tamil south
events.text: The Alvars (Vishnu) and Nayanars (Shiva) sing in Tamil, not Sanskrit — passionate devotion, open to anyone.

events.title: The medieval saints
events.text: Kabir, Mirabai, Tulsidas carry the revolution across languages — vernacular devotional poetry becomes the living scripture.

activities.anchor: worked from inside and against the system
activities.caption: call the conversion
activities.name: hindAmbedkarEst

config.prompt: In 1956, B. R. Ambedkar led a mass conversion to Buddhism to exit caste-Hinduism. Roughly how many Dalits converted?
config.why: Roughly 400,000 — one episode in a contest as traditional as the hierarchy: Rammohan Roy (abolition of sati, 1829), Gandhi, Ambedkar. Today caste is constitutionally abolished in India, socially persistent, politically central.
config.context: The reformers worked from inside the tradition and against it at once.

activities.anchor: The tradition structures a whole biography
activities.caption: order the life-cycle rites
activities.name: hindSamskaraOrder

config.prompt: The samskaras mark the passage — order the rites:
items: Upanayana — sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study
Marriage — fire as witness, seven steps together
Cremation — ideally at a sacred river; the body returns to the elements
config.why: Varanasi's burning ghats are the most famous site — Shiva's city, where to die well. The ethical baseline runs through the yamas and niyamas: non-harm (ahimsa), truthfulness, non-stealing, temperance, non-grasping.
